Take a deep breath, Ernesto. Nobody has written anything yet.
Here is the little silver key to the attic door.
Does the attic even have a proper bed?
Yes, a good wooden bed, a clean desk, and the best view in the house.
Then why do we never rent it to guests?
Because the stairs are narrow and Ernesto keeps old lamp boxes there.

lines.trans: Only three small boxes! Maybe four!
We can move four boxes in five minutes. Let us go look at it right now!
Go up the stairs, turn left at the landing, last door at the top.
I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!
Come on, race you to the third floor!
See you later!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Points to a place farther away from both speakers.

examples.text: La farmacia está allí en la esquina.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is over there on the corner.
We lived there for six years.

meanings.note: Covers both renting from a landlord and renting out to a guest.

examples.trans: We rent a room with a balcony.

examples.text: Ellos alquilaron un piso cerca del río.
examples.trans: They rented a flat near the river.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Tall storage closet or bedroom wardrobe.

examples.trans: The wardrobe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los armarios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wardrobes from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.trans: It is a white piece.

examples.text: Mira, hay un sobre blanco doblado en el asa.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Top-floor room with sloping roof beams.

examples.trans: The attic room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las buhardillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the attic rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox; la caja also means the cash register/box.

examples.trans: The box is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cajas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boxs from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la cama = to make the bed.

examples.trans: The bed is here.

examples.text: Vemos las camas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the beds from the door.

meanings.note: Buena carrera = good run.

examples.trans: The run is here.

examples.text: Vemos las carreras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the runs from the door.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.trans: The house is here.

examples.text: Vemos las casas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the houses from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?
Since then she works with us.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Writing desk in a room or study.

examples.trans: The desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escritorios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the desks from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Opposite of ancho (wide).

examples.trans: It is a narrow piece.

examples.text: Coge la segunda calle, junto al puesto de flores, no el callejón estrecho.
examples.trans: Take the second street, beside the flower stall, not the narrow alley.

meanings.note: De cinco estrellas = five-star.

examples.trans: The star is here.

examples.text: Vemos las estrellas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stars from the door.

meanings.note: Gira a la izquierda = turn left.

examples.text: Gira a la izquierda después del puente.
examples.trans: Turn left after the bridge.

examples.text: Giró la llave dos veces con cuidado.
examples.trans: She turned the key twice carefully.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = take a deep breath.

examples.trans: It is a deep piece.

examples.text: Respire hondo, Ernesto. Todavía nadie ha escrito nada.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath, Ernesto. Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a horrible piece.

examples.text: ¡Treinta y cinco minutos! ¡Va a escribir una reseña horrible de una estrella!
examples.trans: Thirty-five minutes! He is going to write a terrible one-star review!

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la llave.

examples.trans: The little key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llavecitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the little keys from the door.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Table, ceiling, or reading lamp.

examples.trans: The lamp is here.

examples.text: Vemos las lámparas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lamps from the door.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.
Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.trans: We have the same job.
I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.
There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.
Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Precede the verb alone (nunca llega tarde) or follow no.

examples.text: Nunca he visto ese cofre antes.
examples.trans: I have never seen that chest before.

examples.text: El tren de la mañana nunca llega tarde.
examples.trans: The morning train never arrives late.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

meanings.note: Describes silver metal.

examples.trans: It is a silver piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué alivio! Aquí tiene su llave plateada, Javier.
examples.trans: What a relief! Here is your silver key, Javier.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.
She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Variant of quizá.

examples.text: Quizás olvidó el paraguas en el taxi.
examples.trans: Perhaps she left her umbrella in the taxi.
Maybe we can open tomorrow.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Flat landing between flights of stairs.

examples.trans: The stair landing is here.

examples.text: Vemos los rellanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stair landings from the door.

meanings.note: Travel-guide or guest review.

examples.trans: The review is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reseñas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reviews from the door.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = breathe deeply.

examples.text: Salgo al jardín a respirar aire fresco.
examples.trans: I step into the garden to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: Respiró hondo antes de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: He took a deep breath before ringing the bell.

meanings.note: Collective singular feminine noun in Spanish.

examples.text: La ropa es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The clothes is very important here.
We talk about the clothes.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Used in negative or conditional contexts.

examples.text: No cayó ni siquiera una gota.
examples.trans: Not even a single drop fell.
Rest even just five minutes.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Sábanas limpias = clean sheets.

examples.trans: The bedsheet is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sábanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bedsheets from the door.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Shortens to tercer before masculine singular nouns (el tercer escalón).

examples.trans: It is a third piece.
Come on, race you to the third floor!

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.
It is not twelve o'clock yet.

meanings.note: Treinta y cinco = thirty-five.

examples.text: Nos dan treinta días de plazo.
examples.trans: They give us thirty days' notice.

examples.text: Son las nueve y treinta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is nine thirty-five.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.
Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

vista.gloss: view; sight; eyesight (a la vista = in sight)

meanings.en: view; sight; eyesight (a la vista = in sight)
meanings.note: Buena vista = sharp eyes / a lovely view.

examples.trans: The view is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vistas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the views from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!
